scope: Nominal orbit categories for learning and filtering; SSO is a LEO subtype. Colors do not imply current ephemerides, scheduled acquisitions or data availability.

types.label: SSO · LEO subtype
types.description: A near-polar LEO whose orbital plane precesses to maintain approximately the same local solar crossing time. Seasons, terrain and viewing geometry still change illumination.

types.label: Other LEO
types.description: Low Earth orbits are below about 2,000 km. Many EO missions take roughly 90–120 minutes per orbit. This color groups curated LEO classes other than SSO; choose All LEO in the filter to include SSO.

types.label: Geostationary
types.description: A circular equatorial orbit near 35,786 km, with one sidereal-day period (about 23 h 56 min). It keeps an approximately fixed Earth view; instrument scan cadence is a separate quantity.

types.label: Highly elliptical
types.description: Altitude varies strongly around an ellipse. Molniya-type designs dwell near apogee over high latitudes. Ellipticity alone does not determine the region observed or instrument acquisition schedule.

types.label: Sun–Earth L1
types.description: A trajectory near the Sun–Earth L1 libration point, as used by DSCOVR. Distance from Earth is not a LEO altitude, and an Earth-orbit ring is not a physical L1 trajectory.

types.label: Orbit uncurated
types.description: The orbit has not been verified in this catalog. STAC metadata mentions do not establish orbit geometry. Gray is an explicit knowledge gap, not a class inferred from the spacecraft name.
